2027 Application Guide: Doctoral Program in Medicine
Graduate School of Medicine, the University of Tokyo
This application guide may change. The University of Tokyo website (https://www.m.u-
tokyo.ac.jp/english/daigakuin/apply/appguidemain.html) will continuously announce if there is
any change, so please check the newest information constantly.
Purpose of Education for Research
The purpose of research training in the Graduate School of Medicine is to promote advanced research that
will contribute to breakthroughs in the understanding of the mechanisms of life, to improve health, to contribute
to the struggle against disease, and to foster international leaders in all fields of medicine who are outstanding
scholars and highly creative researchers.
Admission Policy
Consistent with the aims described above, for its PhD programs in the Graduate School of Medicine, the
University of Tokyo seeks students who have the potential to become international leaders in all fields of
medicine through outstanding scholarship and advanced and highly creative research. We seek those who
will, as described above, contribute to the understanding of the mechanisms of life, to preventing, curing, and
recovering from disease, and to promoting and supporting healthy human development.
1. Eligibility criteria
(1) Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from a program to study medicine or dentistry
at a Japanese university by 31 March 2027. (Note 1)
(2) Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from a six-year program to study pharmacy
or veterinary medicine at a Japanese university by 31 March 2027. (Note 1)
(3) Persons who have completed or are expected to complete 18 years of overseas curricular education
(ending with a program in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or veterinary medicine) by 31 March 2027.
(Note 2)
Nota bene: Persons on whom a foreign university has not conferred (and is not expected to confer)
a Bachelor's degree in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, or veterinary medicine provided they meet
the conditions related to the restrictions described in (7) or (8) below, and after undergoing individual
eligibility review to determine whether their academic ability is equivalent or superior to that of
graduates of a program of study in medicine, etc., at a Japanese university, may be granted eligibility
to take the entrance examination -- provided that, before applying, they have undergone the
[individual] eligibility review whose application procedure requirements are described in Note 6 and
Note 7 below.
(4) Persons who have been conferred or are expected to be conferred a degree equivalent to that of a
bachelor's degree from a foreign university or other foreign institution of higher education (restricted to
those whose comprehensive status of education and research activities has been assessed by the
government of the said foreign country or a related organization) by March 31, 2027, having completed
a program (restricted to a program to study veterinary medicine, medicine, pharmacy or dentistry) which
requires at least five years of study. (Note 2)
Nota bene: Persons on whom degrees have been conferred (or are expected to be conferred) by a
foreign university with a five-year program of study and whose final program of study is neither
medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nor veterinary medicine, are not eligible to apply under the conditions
1
described here. This notwithstanding however, provided they meet the conditions related to such
restrictions described in (7) or (8) below, after undergoing individual eligibility review to determine
whether their academic ability is equivalent or superior to that of graduates of a program of study in
medicine, etc., at a Japanese university, may be granted eligibility to take the entrance examination -
- provided that, before applying, they have undergone the [individual] eligibility review whose
application procedure requirements are described in Note 6 and Note 7 below.
(5) Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from an educational institution designated by
the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology by March 31, 2027. (Note 3)
(6) Persons who have graduated from a master’s program, etc. (Note 4) at a Japanese university and are
recognized by the Graduate School of Medicine based on an eligibility review as having academic
ability equivalent to or surpassing that of a person who has graduated from a program in medicine,
etc. (Note 5) at a Japanese university. (Note 1)
(7) Persons who have engaged or are expected in research for 2 years or more at a university or a research
institute by March 31, 2027 after graduating from a Japanese university (excluding programs in medicine,
dentistry, or pharmacy or veterinary medicine) or completing 16 years of overseas curricular education
and are recognized by the Graduate School of Medicine based on an eligibility review as having
academic ability equivalent to or surpassing that of a person who has completed a program in medicine,
etc. (Note 5) at a Japanese university. (Note 1) (Note 6)
Nota bene: This clause pertains to persons with documented evidence of two or more years'
employment doing research at a university or a research institute etc.
(8) Persons who are recognized by the Graduate School of Medicine based on an individual eligibility review
as having academic ability equivalent to or surpassing that of a Japanese university graduate, and who
are aged 24 years or older on 31 March 2027. (Note 7)
Nota bene: This clause pertains to persons on whom a Master's degree has been conferred by a foreign
university; note that, before applying for admission, applicants must undergo an individual eligibility
review (Note 7).
Note also that applicants' Bachelor's degree may have been conferred irrespectively either by a
Japanese or by a foreign university.
Nota bene: Clause (7) above, not this clause, pertains to persons with documented evidence of two or
more years' employment doing research at a university or a research institute etc.
Note 1:”Japanese university” mentioned in Eligibilities (1), (2), (6) (7), and (8) above is a university within the boundaries
of Japan and as prescribed in Article 83 of the School Education Law.
Note 2: Eligibilities (3) and (4) above include the case of having completed a distance education program provided by a
foreign school of said country while residing in Japan.
Note 3: “Persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from an educational institution designated by the
Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology” as per eligibility criterion (5) are as follows:
① Persons who have studied medicine or dentistry at the medical or dentistry faculty of a university prescribed
by the old University Ordinance and who have graduated from either of these faculties.
② Persons who have graduated from the National Defense Medical College under the Act for Establishment of
the Ministry of Defense.
③ Persons who have completed a program of a foreign university (restricted to those who have competed 18
years of bachelor’s education in the school education system of said foreign country, ending with a program
either in veterinary medicine, medicine, pharmacy or dentistry) while in Japan, the said program having been
designated separately by the Minister for Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology and belonging
to an educational institution under the school education system of the said foreign country.
2
Note 4: “Persons who have completed a master’s program, etc. at a Japanese university” as per eligibility criterion (6)
are as follows:
① Persons who have completed a master's program or a professional degree program at a Japanese university
and those who are eligible to be conferred a master's degree.
② Persons who have been enrolled for at least two years in a doctoral program which is not separated into
former and latter parts, and have obtained at least 30 academic credits in addition to the required research
guidance at a Japanese university.
Nota bene: Applicants are considered eligible if either ① or ② above pertain; prior review of their entrance
examination eligibility is not required.
Note 5: ”A program in medicine, etc. at a Japanese university” mentioned in Eligibility (6), (7) and (8) above is an
undergraduate program at a Japanese university as follows:
① A program to study medicine
② A program to study dentistry
③ A program to study pharmacy whose main purpose is to cultivate practical clinical ability
④ A program to study veterinary medicine
Note 6: Persons who intend to apply for admission under eligibility criteria (7) above must first undergo an eligibility
review. To undergo the eligibility review, it is necessary for applicants to contact the Administration Office (refer
to 6(4) below) in advance and to submit the required documents to the Office by Thursday, 11 June, 2026.
Persons who are deemed by the Graduate School of Medicine on the basis of an eligibility review to have
academic ability equivalent or superior to that of a university graduate described in eligibility criteria (1) or (2)
shall be permitted to take the entrance exam upon application.
Eligibility review result will be notified by Email around late June, 2026.
Note 7:  Eligibility criterion (8) above is intended for those who do not fall under eligibility criteria (1) - (7) and have
graduated from/completed a program to study medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or veterinary medicine at an
educational institution that is equivalent to a six-year university, and have been deemed by the Graduate School
of Medicine on the basis of an individual eligibility review to have academic ability equivalent or superior to that
of a university graduate described in eligibility criteria (1) or (2).
Persons who intend to apply for admission under eligibility criterion (8) above must first undergo an individual
eligibility review. To undergo the individual eligibility review, it is necessary for applicants to contact the
Administration Office (refer to 6(4) below) in advance and to submit the required documents to the Office by
Thursday, 11 June, 2026.
 Persons who are deemed by the Graduate School of Medicine on the basis of an individual eligibility review to
have academic ability equivalent or superior to that of a university graduate described in eligibility criteria (1) or
(2), shall be permitted to take the entrance exam upon application.
Eligibility review result will be notified by Email around late June, 2026.
2. Admission criteria
Admission shall be determined based on a comprehensive judgement of the academic
performance of the school they came from, the results of other documents screening, written
examination and oral exam and so on.

4. Exam dates & venues
(1) Written exam: Thursday, 15 October 2026
(2) Oral exam: Friday, 16 October 2026
(3) Details of the exam schedules and venues will be given in the 'Entrance Examination Guideline which
will be sent by Email in the middle of September, 2026.
5. Announcement of successful applicants & admission procedures
(1) A list of successful applicants will be posted on the website (http://www.m.u-tokyo.ac.jp/index.html) at
noon on Friday, 20 November 2026.
(2) Those who pass the examinations will receive an admission certificate via the Web Application System
in late November 2026. Instructions on how to receive the certificate will be announced on the Graduate
School’s website, so please be sure to check it.
(3) Admission Certificate recipients are required to complete the necessary admission procedures (i.e.,
payment of admission fees and submission of admission forms) in accordance with the Admission
6
Procedure Guide that will be sent to the Email address indicated in the application form in late February
within designated period on early-March 2027. Failure to complete the admission procedures shall be
regarded as refusal of admission.
(4) Estimated costs of admission in 2027
(International students with a Japanese Government [Monbukagakusho] Scholarship are exempt from

6. Application procedure
(1) ・Applicants must contact faculty member before applying.
・Applicants must declare at the time of application if they have a familial relationship (within two
degrees of kinship, including cohabitation or shared livelihood) with a faculty member in the intended
field of specialization, including the prospective supervisor, or if they are currently employed full-time
and their employer has a conflict of interest (COI) with the intended field.
Such declarations will not be used for admission selection and will be used only to ensure fairness
and for COI management after enrollment.
If any such relationship arises after application, it must be reported promptly to the Administration
Office (refer to 6(4) below).
(2) Applications must be submitted online. For details, please refer to the Graduate School’s website.
(URL: https://www.m.u-tokyo.ac.jp/daigakuin/apply/appguidemain.html)
(3) Application period
From Friday, July 3, 2026, until 11:59 PM on Tuesday, July 14, 2026 (JST).
Research Students ( Monbukagakusho Scholarship students) scheduled to arrive in Japan in autumn
2026 must first contact the Administration Office (see 6(4) below for contact details).

7. Other important points
(1) The examination card will be issued in early July 2026 via your My Page on the Web Application System;
please print it out and bring it with you on the day of the examination. The "Notes on the Examination"
will be sent separately to the email address provided in your application. If you cannot confirm these
by mid-September, contact our office (indicated in section 6.(4)) for instructions.
(2) If you select a written exam subject other than that specified for your desired major, the exam will be
invalid.
(3) Following the submission of application documents, changes to the documents or the refund of exam
fees will not be allowed under any circumstances. Once application documents are received, they are
not returnable.
(4) Those who wish to maintain their employment at a government office, school, hospital, or private
company during enrollment are required to submit a consent form (format optional) from their employer
when completing the admission procedures (see 5(3) above), to the effect that they will remain
committed to their studies while enrolled.
(5) International students are required to obtain the appropriate visa according to the Immigration Control
and Refugee Recognition Act (Cabinet Order No. 319 of 1951) prior to undertaking the admission
procedures.
(6) Admission fees shall not be refunded under any circumstances following the completion of admission
procedures.
(7) The University of Tokyo provides reasonable accommodations to ensure that individuals with disabilities
are not disadvantaged during entrance examinations and studies after enrollment, and provides
consultations for this purpose. Those who wish to request accommodations for entrance examinations
should contact the administrative office indicated in section 6.(4) by 11 June, 2026. Although requests
made after the above deadline will still be considered, it is recommended that applicants send their
requests well in advance as it may not be possible to provide certain accommodations without sufficient
preparation time. (Please refer to the following website for more details: https://www.m.u-
tokyo.ac.jp/daigakuin/apply/appguidemain.html )
(8) Names, addresses, or other personal information obtained from applications will only be used for: 
screening of applicants (application processing & screening);  the announcement of successful
applicants; and  tasks related to admission procedures. This personal information will also be used
for:  academic affairs (enrollment records, learning etc.);  student support (health management,
employment assistance, applications for scholarships and exemption from tuition fees, use of libraries,
etc.); and  collection of tuition fees.
(9) If any false statement or forgery in the application documents, or if there is clear evidence that there
was any fraudulent activity during the examination, that student’s admittance may be canceled even
after enrolling in or going on to a graduate school.
(10) The examination results used in the selection of entrants may be used in future studies for the
improvement of both the entrance examination and the education at the University of Tokyo.
(11) The University of Tokyo has established the “The University of Tokyo Security Export Control
Regulations” in accordance with Japan’s “Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act”, and rigorously
implements security export control for potential students before and after their enrollment on the basis
of these regulations. In particular, pre-enrollment screenings are mandatory for all international
students and also for Japanese students in certain circumstances.
Please be aware that applicants who fall under any of the conditions set out in the Act may not receive
permission to enroll at the university or may have their research activities restricted after their
enrollment even if they have passed the entrance examinations.
